title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Revenue is an opinion; operating cash flow after working-capital absorption and stock-based compensation is the forensic truth.
epigraph.author: Institutional Accounting Forensics

web_blocks.html: From FY2017 through FY2026 (fiscal years ended late January), NVIDIA delivered a historic financial transformation [18, 19]. Revenue compounded 31.2x from $6.91 billion (FY17) to $215.94 billion (FY26) [18, 19]. Over the same span, GAAP net income expanded 71.9x from $1.67 billion to $120.07 billion [18, 19]. This was real cash, not paper profit. Cumulative free cash flow over FY24–FY26 alone reached $184.55 billion ($27.02B + $60.85B + $96.68B) [19]. Q3 FY27 added another $43.78 billion in a single quarter [3].

web_blocks.caption: NVIDIA 10-Year Audited Financial Forensics (FY2017–FY2026, $ Billions)
web_blocks.takeaway: Cash conversion (FCF/Net Income) averaged ~85% during hyper-growth (FY24–FY26) because working capital (AR and inventory) absorbed cash to fund 65%–126% annual revenue expansion; ROIC reached 74.23% TTM [18, 19].

web_blocks.html: Working-Capital & Balance-Sheet Forensics: Two forensic items merit close scrutiny in Q3 FY27. First, Accounts Receivable climbed from $38.47 billion at FY26 year-end to $81.03 billion on October 25, 2026 [3, 4]. That 111% nine-month jump implies roughly 63–65 days sales outstanding on a $115.8B quarterly run-rate [3]. Second, Inventories rose from $21.40 billion (FY26) to $39.72 billion (Q3 FY27) [3, 4]. That build supports the Vera Rubin NVL72 ramp and Q4's $130B revenue guide [3]. Even with that working-capital absorption, Q3 FY27 CFO hit $48.25 billion and FCF reached $43.78 billion [3]. On the balance sheet, NVIDIA holds $53.5 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable debt securities ($29.09B cash + $24.42B debt securities) [3]. It also holds $44.22 billion in marketable equity securities against $32.37 billion in long-term debt on October 25, 2026 (up from $7.47B at FY26 year-end after $24.90B of 9M FY27 debt issuance and $1.0B Q3 repayment; Debt/Equity 0.12x on $266.67B equity, Current Ratio 4.08x) [3, 4].

SBC, Dilution & Capital Return Discipline: Unlike many Silicon Valley peers, NVIDIA's buybacks have outpaced stock-based compensation (SBC). In FY2026, SBC totaled $6.39 billion, or just 3.0% of revenue [4, 11]. Meanwhile, share repurchases totaled $39.04 billion plus $6.29 billion in dividends [4, 11]. Split-adjusted diluted shares steadily shrank from 25.07 billion (FY22) to 24.36 billion (FY26) [19]. In Q3 FY27, NVIDIA returned another $28.1 billion ($22.12B buybacks, $6.03B dividends) [1, 3]. It also expanded its buyback authorization by $150 billion, leaving $227.3 billion available [1, 3].

web_blocks.company: Qualcomm (3G/4G/5G Handset Royalty & SoC Compounding Cycle)
web_blocks.mechanism: Combined fabless SoC scale with a foundational IP/software ecosystem to earn >55%–60% gross margins and high ROIC, returning excess FCF via aggressive buybacks while funding multi-year R&D cycles.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Generated >$10B+ annual FCF with net-cash balance sheets, though handset saturation and customer vertical integration (Apple modem) periodically compressed top-line growth.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: NVIDIA's 74.23% ROIC, 0.14x Debt/Equity, and $227.3B buyback authorization reflect peak fabless capital efficiency, but hyperscaler custom silicon (Broadcom/Marvell) poses a long-term vertical-integration risk analogous to Apple's modem push.

web_blocks.title: Forensic Clean Bill of Health — With One Working-Capital Watch
paragraphs: NVIDIA's balance sheet is a fortress: $53.5B in cash and debt securities plus $44.2B in equity investments sit against $32.37B in long-term debt. Diluted share count is shrinking, and FCF-to-Net-Income conversion exceeds 80%. The sole accounting watchpoint is whether $81.03B in AR, $39.72B in inventory, and $668B in off-balance-sheet commitments and credit-support guarantees convert cleanly into cash in Q4 FY27 and FY28 [3, 9].

web_blocks.html: Off-Balance-Sheet Guarantees & Private-Equity Book Forensics (Q3 FY27): Beyond the $32.37 billion in on-balance-sheet long-term debt, two footnote exposures grew dramatically in 9M FY27. First, non-marketable securities nearly tripled from $22.25 billion (Jan 25, 2026) to $65.53 billion ($61.65B non-marketable equity securities) on October 25, 2026, following $58.10 billion in 9M FY27 equity purchases; Q3 FY27 included $1.85 billion in impairments and unrealized losses on private holdings, while $25.7 billion of publicly held equity securities carry lock-up restrictions ($21.0B short-term, $4.7B through Dec 2027). Second, total off-balance-sheet obligations reached $668 billion: $518 billion in supply, cloud, uncommenced lease, equity, and CapEx commitments ($222B due FY28), $32 billion in neocloud agreements, and $118.0 billion in credit support guarantees—dominated by $105.0 billion for SB Energy's Ohio campus hosting OpenAI under 20-year leases.

book_paragraphs: Numbers don't lie, and when you and I lay out NVIDIA's ten-year financial statement side by side from FY2017 to FY2026, two truths jump off the page. The first is the sheer scale of operating leverage: revenue grew 31-fold from $6.91 billion to $215.94 billion, while GAAP net income grew 72-fold from $1.67 billion to $120.07 billion. In the last three fiscal years alone, NVIDIA generated $184.55 billion in free cash flow—and then added $43.78 billion more in Q3 FY27.

The second truth is what happens to cash conversion during hyper-growth. In FY2026, NVIDIA converted 80.5% of its $120.07 billion net income into free cash flow ($96.68 billion). Why wasn't it 100%? Because when you are scaling from $130.5 billion to $215.9 billion—and then toward $130 billion a quarter—you have to finance receivables and inventory upfront. By Q3 FY27, accounts receivable reached $81.03 billion and inventories hit $39.72 billion. That is normal for a business doubling year-over-year, provided DSO stays near 63–65 days and customers pay on time.

Look at the balance sheet backing that working capital: $53.5 billion in cash and marketable debt securities, plus another $44.2 billion in marketable equity securities, sitting against $32.37 billion of long-term debt (following $24.90 billion of new debt issued in 9M FY27). That is a fortress.

Two major footnote expansions in Q3 FY27 also demand attention: non-marketable securities nearly tripled to $65.53 billion (including a $1.85 billion Q3 impairment/unrealized loss), and off-balance-sheet obligations expanded to $668 billion—comprising $518 billion in commitments, $32 billion in neocloud agreements, and $118.0 billion in credit support guarantees led by $105.0 billion for SB Energy's Ohio campus hosting OpenAI.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The cleanest forensic test of management discipline in Silicon Valley is comparing share buybacks against stock-based compensation. In FY2026, NVIDIA spent $6.39 billion on SBC (just 3% of revenue) and bought back $39.04 billion of stock, shrinking diluted shares from 25.07 billion in FY22 to 24.36 billion in FY26. Shareholders aren't being diluted—they are being concentrated, even before we ever look at a stock price.

book_subsections.title: ROIC, Capital Allocation & What Could Break the Cash Engine
paragraphs: With trailing twelve-month ROIC sitting at 74.23% and CapEx running under 3% of revenue, NVIDIA has far more cash than its core business can reinvest. Management's response has been straightforward: fund $18.5 billion a year in R&D, lock up HBM4 and CoWoS-L supply, and return the rest—$28.1 billion in Q3 FY27 alone—through buybacks and dividends, backed by a fresh $150 billion buyback authorization.

What could break this cash machine? Not debt, and not SBC dilution. The only real balance-sheet vulnerability is an unexpected demand air-pocket colliding with $39.72 billion of on-hand inventory and $390 billion of multi-year supply commitments. As long as Q4 FY27 hits its $130 billion target and FY28 scales as guided, cash conversion will remain extraordinary.

Finally, keep an eye on the $44.22 billion in marketable equity securities sitting on NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 balance sheet alongside its $53.5 billion in cash and debt securities. In FY2026, non-operating income—driven by $2.30 billion in interest income and ~$9.02 billion in investment gains—added over $11 billion to pre-tax profit. As NVIDIA invests in AI cloud partners and ecosystem startups, mark-to-market equity swings will increasingly flow through GAAP net income, making operating income and free cash flow even cleaner yardsticks of core business health.
